new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the last syllable of every word (mono-, sesqui-, di- and trisyllabic words alike); it is non-contrastive, and there is no tone or register contrast.
new_statements.exceptions: None for words. Related remarks: proclitics are bound forms that cannot receive stress (sec. 3.2.4, p. 517); fully reduplicated adverbs/interrogatives do not conform to word constraints or word-level stress patterns and are not treated as words (sec. 3.2.5, p. 518); vowels in open word-final syllables are phonetically lengthened (pp. 507-508).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('words'), stated in the phonology sketch of a grammar-sketch-style language profile; based on the authors' fieldwork at Sungai Rual (Jeli, Kelantan). Not instrumental.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes Jedek of Sungai Rual (Jeli, Kelantan), the only known Jedek community (~280 speakers), i.e. jede1239 itself; Glottolog classes it as Northern Aslian, Menraq-Batek subgroup. The earlier scan's citation '2018, Linguistic Typology 22(3)' is incorrect: the article is 2017, 21(3): 493-545 (Crossref, LUP and the thesis reprint agree).

Sec. 3.2.4 p. 517: clitics (all proclitics) cannot receive stress; sec. 3.2.5 p. 518: full reduplications do not conform to word-level stress patterns; pp. 507-508: vowels of open final syllables are phonetically lengthened.
